subject: Region-aware SLA bundles & credits — packaging questions
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the conversation last week — Orbital Health is evaluating Redwood for a multi-region inference deployment and we need clarity on how SLA and premium support packaging would work across regions. Two quick asks to start:

1) How do you price and package uptime tiers when we require active-active failover between US-East and EU-West? Specifically, are there distinct "failover credits" or a blended tier?
2) What's the typical discounting approach for a 12–18 month commit at ~$1.2M ARR? We need a clear view of response windows, escalation coverage (onsite vs remote — we expect remote triage + callback), and how credits would apply if failover triggers a cross-region switchover.

Can you put together an initial packaging suggestion and a sample pricing worksheet?

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Platform Engineering
Orbital Health

Attachment: usage_profile_q1_2027.csv (text/csv)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've started a draft pricing worksheet and a short note on packaging options (attached). High level — we typically do:

- Blended availability tiers: single SLA applied to the committed footprint, with a built-in cross-region failover allowance (the "failover buffer").
- Failover credits: applied when a failover causes sustained increased consumption above the buffer for >30 minutes; credits scale by excess token-hours and a pre-agreed multiplier depending on severity.
- Response windows: Standard (8x5), Priority (24x7), and Premium (24x7 with on-call retainer). Escalation coverage mapping is configurable per-region.

I'll attach: Orbital_SLA_Pricing_worksheet_v3.xlsx and a compact term sheet. Could you send a short summary of expected peak concurrency and whether you need on-prem private endpoints in EU region? That will change the pricing materially.

If useful, we can set a 30-min sync tomorrow to run through the workbook.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Kimberly —

Thanks, received both attachments. Quick clarification on our side:

- Peak concurrency is ~1,600 vCPU-equivalent inference sessions, sustained bursts to ~3,500 for up to 45 minutes.
- Monthly token volume estimate ~120M tokens.
- We will not be running on-prem in EU initially — everything will be cloud-based but we require EU data residency for EU-region model keys.
- Primary ask: a 12-month commitment. Our procurement team wants to understand the magnitude of "failover buffer" and the crediting thresholds (so they can evaluate risk).

Can Karthik or finance give a sample calculation that converts a failover event into an expected credit figure? Also: what discount band should we expect for this TCV?

Cheers,
Elena

Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits — request for sample credit calc and discount band

Team — looping you in for pricing calc and discount guidance. Key details from Orbital: 1.2M ARR target/12-month commit, monthly ~120M tokens, peak concurrency up to 3.5k for short bursts, cloud-only (EU residency required).

Proposed approach (draft):
- Option A (Conservative): 99.95% blended uptime across committed footprint, built-in failover buffer = 10% of committed consumption per region, failover credits apply to excess >10% sustained >30m. Estimated credit exposure per 1 hour failover event = 0.5% of monthly committed spend (example numbers in attached worksheet).
- Option B (Premium): 99.99% with a dedicated retainer (on-call) + 24x7 priority support; smaller failover buffer (5%) and quicker escalation SLA. Price uplift +12% to +18% depending on retainer size.

Asking Finance: Laura — can you produce a sample failure-to-credit calculation using their volumes and give us a discount band for TCV ~1.2M (what's realistic for an enterprise pilot -> committed rollout)?

Elena — we'll get a calculation back by EOD tomorrow and propose two concrete SKU packs. If that looks good, we can get a pilot addendum and DocuSign ready.

Thanks,
Kim

Attachment: Orbital_SLA_Pricing_worksheet_v3.xlsx
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ORBITAL-1245

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits — request for sample credit calc and discount band

Kim/Karthik/Elena —

Attached is a short worked example (sheet tab "CreditCalc") using Orbital's token volumes and peak concurrency. Key takeaways:

- Using Option A assumptions, a 2-hour sustained cross-region failover that pushes consumption 18% above buffer would translate to approximately 1.1% credit on that month's invoice (~$11,000 on a $1M monthly run-rate equivalent). The credit escalates non-linearly if failover persists beyond 4 hours.
- Option B reduces exposure materially (example shows ~0.2% credit for same event) due to the larger retainer and faster triage.
- Discounting: For a 12-month, $1.2M ARR commit, we can offer an ELA-style band: 10% standard discount + up to 5% for annual payment and technical onboarding credit (total up to 15%). For pilot-first then convert to commit within 90 days, we can offer a 7% pilot discount and an execution credit applied at conversion.

If Orbital needs an even firmer cap on credit exposure we can structure a capped credit reserve (pre-funded retainer) at an incremental cost.

Laura Bennett
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Orbital_SLA_Pricing_worksheet_v3.xlsx (updated with CreditCalc tab)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits — next steps

Elena — thanks for the details and thanks Laura for the calc. To be pragmatic:

- Proposal: Start with a 3-month pilot (7% pilot discount) scoped to US + EU with Option A packaging and a capped credit exposure via a $25k pilot-recovery retainer.
- On successful pilot metrics (latency/availability and failover behaviour), convert to 12-month committed ELA with 12% baseline discount + 3% accelerated payment credit (total 15%) and optional on-call retainer for Premium OPTION B if you want tighter exposure.
- We'll prepare a pilot addendum and a full-term sheet for the commit phase; DocuSign links can be shared once Orbital confirms the pilot SKU.

If that aligns I'll have legal prep the addendum and Kimberly will coordinate signatures.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
